page: Microsoft Azure D96alds_v7 is an x86_64 compute-focused instance belonging to the low-memory Daldsv7 series. It is powered by a 4.5 GHz AMD EPYC 9V45 processor delivering 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is configured at 192.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Virtualized under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance includes modern instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and cryptographic acceleration through AES and SHA-NI.

For local disk performance, the instance features 5669 GB of integrated NVMe SSD storage. It does not include dedicated hardware GPU acceleration. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate top-tier compute and throughput execution, recording 175877.61 on stress-ng multi-core, 3725.27 on single-core, and a PassMark CPU score of 116904.05. Memory subsystems deliver 309.38 GB/sec in large uncached reads and 173.94 GB/sec in writes. In operational tests, the configuration attained 139.48 million Redis SET operations per second and 93.44 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance provides high compute density and extensive NVMe capacity without the cost premium associated with standard 4:1 RAM-to-vCPU footprints or discrete GPUs. The primary tradeoff lies in the restricted 2.0 GB memory per core allocation, which constrains workloads that require massive in-memory datasets. Consequently, the instance is well suited for CPU-intensive data batch processing, compilation pipelines, high-throughput caching, web servers, and local scratchpad database engines.
description: Microsoft Azure D96alds_v7 is an x86_64 instance powered by a 4.5 GHz AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores. Configured with a 1:2 compute-optimized ratio, it supplies 192.0 GB of system memory alongside 5669 GB of bundled NVMe SSD storage. Benchmark results show leading performance across multi-threaded computational workloads, achieving top-tier ratings in stress-ng tests, PassMark CPU evaluation, and cryptographic operations. In real-world service simulations, it delivers 139.48 million operations per second in Redis and 93.44 GB/sec in static web throughput. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V without GPU accelerators, it maximizes throughput-per-core economics for applications where heavy RAM allocations are unnecessary. This hardware profile aligns with high-concurrency web serving, large-scale software compilation, distributed database engines requiring low-latency local storage, and parallel compute tasks.
